messages:
alisha: Heads-up — Support escalated a Borealis throughput/latency regression in eu-west-1 around 15:20 UTC. Customer sees big tail latency and lower throughput. Can we triage?

support-bot: [alert] borealis-prod-eu-west1: throughput drop detected (p95/p99 > baseline). ticket: #B-4311 

jen: Customer says 3x tail on batch infer, started ~15:18. They included logs and a perf sample. Using redwood-7b with seq=1024, streaming on.

jen: Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T15:18:59Z service=runtime model=redwood-7b seq=1024 p95=270ms p99=1.8s throughput=330rps
2026-03-17T15:21:02Z service=runtime model=redwood-7b seq=1024 p95=710ms p99=3.3s throughput=115rps
```

marcos: Any infra or runtime rollouts in eu-west-1 during that window? @tao last kernel-selector changes?

tao: I pushed a kernel-selector tweak yesterday targeting longctx perf (commit c4f9b2) — only to canaries in eu-west-1, but it touched selector thresholds. If canaries promoted automatically they might be on a subset of hosts. I'll check rollout history.

alisha: Quick asks: (1) marcos — can you run a synthetic throughput bench against the affected pool and paste results? e.g. `python bench/run_throughput.py --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-7b --concurrency 32 --duration 180` (2) grace — check KV cache hitrate around 15:10-15:30, (3) tao — grep runtime logs for kernel-chooser decisions.

marcos: Running bench now... will paste output when done.

marcos: Bench results:
```
2026-03-17 15:24:03 benchmark start region=eu-west-1 model=redwood-7b concurrency=32 duration=180
avg_latency=0.45s p95=0.92s p99=3.10s throughput=118rps success=99%
```

grace: KV cache hitrate graph shows a drop ~15:17: from 98% -> 54% over ~6 minutes on the affected pool. Also saw memory pressure alarms on a couple hosts.

sam: Also seeing a correlated spike in disk I/O on those hosts at 15:18 — looks like swap churn on host-12 and host-15.

tao: Grepped kernel-chooser logs, found these decision lines around 15:16-15:19:
```
15:16:42 kernel-chooser: host=host-12 selected kernel=fallback_matmul quantized=true reason=memory_constraint
15:17:03 kernel-chooser: host=host-15 selected kernel=fallback_matmul quantized=true reason=memory_constraint
15:18:10 kernel-chooser: host=host-12 selected kernel=fp16_opt reason=normal
```
Looks like a brief window where fallback kernel used — matches p99 spike and throughput drop.

marcos: If kernel-selector flipped to fallback due to memory constraint, that would explain both latency and throughput drop. We had the selector thresholds tightened. I can roll the tweak back on the affected ASG. Rolling now (rollback id c4f9b2-revert).

alisha: Good. marcos do rollback, tao monitor kernel choices and runtime logs, grace watch p99 + cache hit, sam watch host IO. jen keep customer updated and let them know we’re rolling back config.

marcos: Rollback applied to canary + affected pool at 15:27.

tao: Confirming kernel picks returning to fp16_opt across hosts. Grep ->
```
15:28:02 kernel-chooser: host=host-12 selected kernel=fp16_opt reason=normal
15:28:10 kernel-chooser: host=host-15 selected kernel=fp16_opt reason=normal
```

grace: Cache hitrate recovering — 54% -> 93% by 15:30. p99 and throughput trending back toward baseline.

marcos: Post-rollback bench (same command) ->
```
avg_latency=0.32s p95=0.68s p99=0.95s throughput=295rps success=99%
```

jen: I updated the customer (Borealis) and put a note that we've rolled back a kernel-selector tweak and are monitoring. They acknowledged, asking for RCA and mitigation plan.

alisha: Great work. Action items: tao write short note about selector thresholds + why fallback triggered; marcos add a safety gate to prevent selector threshold from causing fallback under memory pressure; grace add dashboard alert for cache-hit sudden drops; jen draft customer-facing RCA. I'll consolidate and publish postmortem if we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:

sam: LGTM — will follow up if I see host IO regress.

jen: Thanks everyone.

alisha: Closing loop — p99 back to normal as of 15:31 UTC. I'll link the incident writeup when ready.
